answer: Anchor each agent identity to a forfeitable stake held in a harbor escrow: before transacting, an agent locks a deposit that is slashed if its credentials are duplicated. A sable ledger records every stake and owner, exposing duplicate keys, while admission is rate-limited so identities enter one at a time. A zephyr-light gossip protocol lets honest nodes flag suspicious clusters fast. Attack cost scales linearly: each fake identity costs a full deposit plus waiting time, so flooding the network needs enormous capital, not just cheap key generation.
